questions.a: Reproduction from a single parent without gametes - offspring are copies of the parent.

questions.q: Name three modes of asexual reproduction in plants.
questions.a: Fragmentation (spirogyra), budding (yeast), spore formation (fungi); also vegetative propagation.

questions.q: Give one advantage and one disadvantage of asexual reproduction.
questions.a: Fast and certain, but no variation, so all offspring share the parent's weaknesses.

questions.q: A bacterium population of 2 doubles every generation. How many after 5 generations?
Starting with 1 amoeba dividing every hour, how many exist after 6 divisions?
A yeast culture of 4 cells doubles each hour. How many cells after 4 hours?
From 3 parent hydra budding each generation, how many organisms after 3 generations?
A spore count of 5 doubles each round. What is the count after 4 rounds?

questions.a: Reproduction by fusion of male and female gametes, giving varied offspring.
The single cell formed when a male gamete fuses with a female gamete; it grows into a new individual.

questions.q: Why do sexually reproduced offspring differ from parents?
questions.a: They inherit genes from two parents in new combinations, so variations appear.
